# Mike Holp: AI Automation Station

Mike Holp tests new AI models, agents, and automation tools on real builds and publishes the results on the AI Automation Station YouTube channel. Most videos cover Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and n8n, with every setup step shown. He also builds TubeAnalytics and VisiScan and hosts AI Income Lab, the paid learning community on Skool.

AI Income Lab here means "AI Income Lab by Mike Holp" (skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346). It is not affiliated with other Skool groups or courses that use a similar name.

## Key facts

- Product and membership facts reviewed November 15, 2026 against the published site. Check the linked official pages for subsequent changes.
- New long-form videos most days; the full archive is at /videos.
- TubeAnalytics: YouTube analytics for creators. 7-day trial with a card required; plans from $19 a month.
- VisiScan: checks whether AI assistants recommend a business. Free scan with no signup; full report $49 USD once; weekly monitoring from $29 USD a month.
- AI Income Lab: Skool community with 2,900+ members. Standard $29, Premium $49, VIP $89 a month, or $290, $490, $890 a year. VIP adds weekly live group coaching and Q&A, software deals, and 6,400+ n8n templates. Coaching is group learning support. Custom business implementation is separate and is not included in membership. Ask about project scope before joining.
- AI Income Lab billing is in USD. Free written guides and videos are separate from the paid Skool membership; automation hosting, AI API usage, and other software can cost extra.
- On Standard, Beginner’s Automation Course unlocks at Skool level 2 and VAPI AI Voice Agent Course at level 4. Premium and VIP include immediate access to both and the Complete AI Avatar Video Course.
- Income is not guaranteed; results depend on the project, experience, and time invested.
- Sponsorship: brands can sponsor a build shown on the channel. Dedicated video $1,500, YouTube Short $400, LinkedIn post $350, AI Income Lab post $300, or all four as a campaign for $2,250 ($2,550 separately). Past sponsored builds include Treg, DataForSEO, BrowserAct, Bluehost and Apify.

- [AI automation guides: Claude Code, Codex, n8n and more](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides.html): Free AI automation guides and articles: learn Claude Code, Codex, Make.com, n8n, AI agents and SEO, with practical builds, sources and checks you can run.
- [Recommended tools](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/tools.html): the AI tools from the YouTube descriptions, grouped by job, each with the videos that use it. The buttons are affiliate or referral links.
- [Start here](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/start-here.html): Choose a free first build: AI API gateways, creator websites, business automation, or avatar and voice agents. Find prerequisites and practical next steps.
- [React YouTube feed tutorial: API, caching and fallbacks](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-feed.html): Build a YouTube feed in React with server-side API access, cached video data, accessible cards and failure checks when a request fails.

- [Build a Chat Web App in Google AI Studio, No Code](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/google-ai-studio-chat-app.html): Build a ChatGPT-style web app in Google AI Studio build mode, connect the OpenAI API, then see what deploying needs. Notes from an Oct 2025 walkthrough.
- [OpenCode Stripe Billing Build: A SaaS Case Study](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-stripe-billing-saas.html): Watch OpenCode add Stripe subscription pages to a SaaS app, fix a Prisma and missing-dependency build, and see what was not tested.
- [n8n Social Post Template: Trends, Research, Posting](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/n8n-social-media-agent-template.html): Import n8n’s multi-social post template, test the Google Trends and keyword steps, and see why the Perplexity and posting steps still failed.
- [n8n WhatsApp AI agent setup guide](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/n8n-whatsapp-ai-agent.html): Build the two-part n8n WhatsApp reply workflow: the trigger, an AI agent on OpenRouter, the Meta app setup, and the verification error left unresolved.
- [Make.com Course: Sheets, OpenAI, Airtable, Facebook](https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-com-beginner-course-scenarios.html): Follow a Make.com beginner course: a Sheets to Gmail template, an OpenAI, Airtable and Facebook scenario with its errors, and an Apollo lead scraper.

# Pricing: AI Income Lab by Mike Holp

Reviewed November 12, 2026. AI Income Lab is the paid learning community on Skool (skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346). Prices are in USD and are charged by Skool. This site never sees payment details. Check the Skool plans page for current prices: https://www.skool.com/ai-automation-station-7346/plans

## Plans

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | $29 | $290 | Self-directed learners building their first workflows and unlocking lessons as they participate |
| Premium | $49 | $490 | Builders ready to make automations, voice agents and avatar videos with immediate course access |
| VIP | $89 | $890 | Builders who want weekly group help with their projects and reusable n8n workflows |

Cancel before the next billing period from your Skool account.

## What each plan includes

- Standard: community, courses and tutorials; Beginner's Automation Course (unlocks at Skool level 2); VAPI AI Voice Agent Course (unlocks at level 4).
- Premium: everything in Standard, immediate access to the Beginner's Automation Course and the VAPI AI Voice Agent Course, and the Complete AI Avatar Video Course.
- VIP: everything in Premium, weekly live group coaching and Q&A, the Ultimate N8N Template Library (6,400+ workflows), and software deals.

## Limits and scope

- Coaching is weekly group coaching and Q&A for members implementing what they learn. Custom business implementation is separate and is not included in membership. Ask about project scope before joining.
- No income is guaranteed.

## Free without joining

All written guides (https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides.html) and YouTube videos are free and need no Skool login. The tools used in the guides may need their own accounts or charge for usage.

## Other products by Mike Holp

- VisiScan (https://visiscan.app): free scan with no signup; full report $49 once; weekly monitoring from $29 a month.
- TubeAnalytics (https://www.tubeanalytics.net): YouTube analytics for creators; 7-day trial with a card required; Starter $19, Professional $49 and Enterprise $149 a month.

## Every written guide, with its quick answer

### 9Router Cost Tracking: Combos and Fallbacks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/9router-cost-tracking-fallbacks.html (updated 2026-11-15)
On 9 July 2026, 9Router ran as a local proxy so OpenCode token use and estimated cost stayed visible, with model combos, auto-fallback from subscription to cheap to free, and weekly quota on the same dashboard. Install is on the 9Router setup guide.

### 9Router: npm install, port 20128, skip-update
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/9router-setup.html (updated 2026-11-19)
9Router is a gateway between your coding tools and their model providers. It gives Claude Code, Codex and similar tools one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, http://localhost:20128/v1, plus a dashboard for providers, keys, model combos and usage. Install it with npm install -g 9router, add one provider and verify one request before adding fallbacks. The default port is 20128; start it with 9router --port 8080 to change it. The CLI checks for updates each time it starts, and Docker users update with docker pull decolua/9router:latest.

### Aegis VPN with Claude Code: Build and Test the Client
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/aegis-vpn-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-19)
Aegis VPN is Mike's WireGuard desktop client, built with Claude Code in Herdr on a Tauri and Rust stack. The first video covers the ChatGPT research, the plan, and an early Linux compile. The next-day follow-up shows a public GitHub repo, imported free Proton test server configs, and the leak, kill switch, and speed checks he ran. The app was Linux-only in that recording. Mike said it was not 100% secure yet. This is one combined guide because the two videos are the same project, not two separate VPN products.

### Free Agent Skills for SEO: Install and Run in Kilo Code
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/agent-skills-seo-kilo-code.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Run npx skills add, scroll the dozens of skills and press space to select, choose Claude Code and Kilo Code as targets, install globally and pick symlink. Then run them on a real site: the image skill flagged a large avatar and images without width and height, the Core Web Vitals skill worked on LCP, CLS and INP, and an IndexNow skill generated a script that submits every URL to Bing, run with npx tsx. A PageSpeed retest showed about the same speed and Core Web Vitals still failing, with desktop at 97.

### How does agentic AI differ from traditional automation?
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/agentic-ai-vs-traditional-automation.html (updated 2026-11-13)
Traditional automation follows a path you drew in advance. Agentic AI is handed a goal and a set of tools, and it decides which steps to take. That difference changes how you build, test and trust the system.

### AI Agent Training Compared: Free Courses and Coaching
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-agent-training-compared.html (updated 2026-11-17)
Good AI agent training should teach you to connect an agent to tools and data, add an approval step and guardrails, and debug failures. You can start free: Zapier Academy has free self-paced courses that include AI agents, Make Academy has an Automation to AI Agents path, and the n8n Academy has a course on AI, testing and best practices. DeepLearning.AI offers short courses on agent techniques, and Maven lists live courses. Pay for coaching only if you want feedback. I run AI Income Lab, so I say where the free options are the better choice.

### AI agent workflow: choose tools, add checks, keep control
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-agent-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-14)
an agent workflow uses a model to choose among steps or tools toward a goal. Start with one bounded task, give it only the tools and data needed, validate its output, and require approval before it sends messages, changes records, spends money or publishes content.

### AI automation agency: sell services to small businesses
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-automation-services-small-business.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Sell one recurring task as a fixed deliverable. Run discovery first, agree acceptance checks before you build, make the record flow work before adding any AI step, price on effort, scope and value, and hand over documentation with a maintenance plan. Skip vague “AI transformation” offers: neither you nor the owner can tell when they are finished.

### AI Automation Strategy Notes: Skills, YouTube SEO, Policy
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-automation-strategy-notes-skills-seo-policy.html (updated 2026-11-15)
The one practical routine is the YouTube SEO one: use a popular custom GPT for YouTube SEO to draft a description from your title, edit it by hand, test titles with a vidIQ score, change one thing at a time and check analytics after a week or two. The other four are talks. One reads reports about YouTube’s July 15, 2025 update on mass-produced and repetitive content, one is my case for learning automation with Make.com, one is a scripted overview of five automation tools and one is a short promo. None shows a result, so I mark them as opinion.

### What Is AI Automation? Examples, Tools and a First Build
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-automation.html (updated 2026-11-11)
AI automation combines rules-based automation with an AI step that classifies, extracts, drafts or decides inside a workflow, so an incoming event can become a checked result and a useful action without someone manually copying information between every stage of the process.

### npx skills: Install Ten Coding Agent Skills
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-coding-agent-skills-top-10.html (updated 2026-11-19)
On 1 June 2026 I installed ten third-party skills from skills.sh with npx and ran them in Codex, OpenCode and VS Code. The registry page showed about 620,000 skills. I updated with npx skills update, then pasted npx skills add from a skill page. The front-end design skill rewrote a light theme. Other runs covered Vercel React and Next.js practices, SEO, AI SEO, PageSpeed and Lighthouse, and GEO content. Quoted install counts and scores are what I showed that day. This is the ten-skill tour, not the free-models OpenCode setup.

### AI Coding Tutorials Compared: Claude Code, OpenCode, More
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-coding-tutorials-compared.html (updated 2026-11-17)
To learn AI-assisted coding, start with the official quickstart for the tool you will use, such as the Claude Code docs or the OpenCode docs, then follow one complete build-along tutorial that shows debugging and cost. freeCodeCamp teaches coding fundamentals for free but is a different goal from working with a coding agent. DeepLearning.AI offers short courses on AI topics. I make build-along tutorials and run a paid community, AI Income Lab, so I say where the free options are the better choice.

### AI content creation workflow: images, video and audio
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-content-creation-workflows.html (updated 2026-11-14)
use AI to draft or transform content, then review every output before publishing. Start with the audience and format, prepare the source material, generate one small draft, check accuracy and rights, and export only after a person approves it.

### AI Implementation Coaching vs Consulting: How to Choose
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-implementation-coaching-guide.html (updated 2026-11-17)
Coaching teaches you to build and run your own automations, a consultant or agency builds them for you, and a large consulting firm usually plans strategy across a company. For a first AI process, start with one repeated task, ask any provider to show working automations like the ten in my Make.com examples video, keep your own accounts and credentials, and choose coaching if you want to maintain the workflows yourself. I offer weekly group coaching in AI Income Lab and separate custom work through my agency, and I explain where each fits.

### AI Model News: Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-model-news-kimi-glm-fable-gemini.html (updated 2026-11-15)
These are release-day notes, so treat benchmark claims as the vendors’ and other creators’ results, not mine. GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3 are selectable in OpenCode on the Go plan with the models command, and I could not run GLM 5.2 myself because I had hit my limit. Kimi K3 was cheaper per token than Claude Fable 5 but, in another creator’s test, used far more tokens and ran longer, and my audit hit a priority-queue limit. Fable 5’s return came with new classifiers that route some coding to Opus 4.8. Gemini 3 in Google AI Studio rebuilt a landing page and a logo mockup app quickly.

### AI side hustles for beginners: 7 services to test
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/ai-side-hustles.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Pick a small service whose output you can check yourself: lead intake, follow-up drafts, recurring reports, spreadsheet cleanup, FAQ drafts, specialist editing or workflow documentation. Judge each by the skill it needs, its startup cost and the time to a first client, then test the closest one this week before paying for tools. None of these are earnings claims.

For which Claude model to pick, see Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku vs Fable.

### Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku vs Fable: which to use
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-models-compared.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Use Claude Opus 5.5 for most coding and agent work: it is Anthropic’s recommended starting point and costs $4 / $20 per million input / output tokens. Use Sonnet 5.5 ($2 / $10) when speed and cost matter more, for well-scoped fixes and frequent coding turns. Use Haiku 5.5 (from $0.10 / $0.50) for high-volume jobs such as classification, extraction and sub-agents. Keep Fable 5.1 ($10 / $50) for the hardest long-running tasks, after Opus 5.5 at a higher effort has fallen short.

### Claude SEO Skill: Audit and Fix a Site From Claude Code
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/claude-seo-skill-site-audit.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Run the one-line curl command from the Claude SEO GitHub page to install the skill files, sub-agents and Python dependencies, then open Claude Code and type a slash to see the new SEO commands. I ran the audit command on tubeanalytics.net, then the plan command with SaaS as the business type, approved fixes for canonicals, title tags and 404s, let it rewrite the sitemap and robots file and ran a GEO analysis. About 20 minutes of work used up my Claude Pro limit twice, and the full audit was interrupted.

### CleanYourTV with Claude Code: TCL Setup and Risks

Check that your TV runs Android TV or Google TV, turn on USB debugging, paste the CleanYourTV prompt into Claude Code and let it back up the TV before it changes anything. On Windows, use the PowerShell installer below. npm (npm install -g @openai/codex) and Homebrew also work. Then run codex in a project folder and choose Sign in with ChatGPT.

### Internal Link Audit with Codex: A Reviewed SEO Workflow
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/codex-seo-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-19)
Give Codex the research you want to apply, ask it to audit your site against that research, and have it write the findings to a report. Turn the report into a phased implementation plan saved in your repo, run the plan with a capable model, then ask Codex to run the same audit again. Review the diff before you deploy. The same loop works for most on-page SEO jobs. In this guide I use internal linking as the example.

In this exercise you add a malformed-JSON request to a local API example and assert that it returns HTTP 400. You need Git, Node.js 22 or later and a configured coding assistant, but no provider key.

### React consent tracking: Google Analytics and Meta
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/consent-tracking.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Ask visitors for a clear choice, store the preference, and route every optional Google Analytics or Meta event through one consent guard so nothing fires before they accept. Give each event a single meaning: an outbound click shows interest, not a sale. Then test that declining keeps every optional tracker off.

### DextroLab: A White-Label Client Portal for Make.com and n8n

### Test your first AI API request locally
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/first-api-request.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Run a local test before calling a real provider: send one request to the example mock server, read the status code, and assert the result. A wrong key should return 401, an unknown model 404 and a valid request 200. The example needs Node.js 22 or later, costs nothing and never reads your API keys.

### Free Claude Code GitHub Setup: NIM and OpenRouter Proxy
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/free-claude-code-setup.html (updated 2026-11-19)
On 5 May 2026 I cancelled Claude Pro, cloned the Free Claude Code GitHub project (about 21,000 to 22,000 stars that day), copied .env.example to .env, added an NVIDIA NIM key from build.nvidia.com and an OpenRouter key, then started the local proxy on port 8082. A test reply used NVIDIA NIM GLM 4.7 and was slower than Pro. I later preferred OpenRouter StepFun 3.5 Flash, which I said was 10 cents per million tokens. A Next.js AI-search app started in a new folder and was not demoed finished. This is the community proxy, not the official Claude Code install.

### Free Claude Code vs OpenCode vs Codex
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/free-claude-code-vs-opencode-codex.html (updated 2026-11-15)
I built an AI search visibility app locally in Next.js using Free Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex, then moved away from Free Claude Code because of repeated API request errors, slow replies and a 401 unauthorized error that came from the order I started the proxy and Claude Code. OpenCode answered quickly on free models, and I preferred Codex at about $20 a month over Claude Pro. This is one project and one person’s experience, not a controlled test.

### GrokBot as a Chief of Staff: Daily Briefings and Approvals
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-chief-of-staff-daily-briefing.html (updated 2026-11-17)
I treated GrokBot as a chief of staff: at the end of the day I asked what ran, what is waiting and what is tomorrow, then pushed each item to a specialist bot instead of doing it myself. In two long conversations it summarised jobs and outreach, queued page speed tests, drafted backlink emails, diagnosed indexing problems, set weekly Monday routines for indexing and Stripe checks, and held drafts until I approved them. The rule that made it safe was simple: reading and drafting are automatic, sending emails and merging code need my explicit yes.

Start a new GrokBot chat for each task, widen routine schedules, pause routines you are not using, move recurring jobs off the bot you chat with all day, and leave on-demand monthly spending off. ### GrokBot for Beginners: First Bot, Access and Approvals
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-for-beginners.html (updated 2026-11-14)
GrokBot gives you AI "bots" that work like teammates. Bots share one persistent Linux box with separate agent desktops and browsers, can run in the background while your laptop is closed, and can save a workflow as a routine. To start, install the app, create one bot with a narrow job, connect only the apps it needs, require explicit approval for anything that sends or posts, and turn the task into a routine once it works twice.

### GrokBot for SEO: Audit Bots, Data and Reviewed Fixes
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-for-seo.html (updated 2026-11-19)
Import a site audit bot and an SEO bot from the GrokBot marketplace, give them your domain, and let them set up recurring audits as routines. Connect a keyword data source, such as Treg or a plugin like Ahrefs, so the bots work from real search data. Then ask for a full audit and a content plan, and send the fixes to a coding agent with a review step before anything ships.

### GrokBot job application agent setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-job-application-agent.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In GrokBot, talk to a Chief of Staff bot. Upload a resume, let a job-app agent pull matching roles, attach the reviewed resume to queued drafts, and keep outbound applications for your approval. This walkthrough queued work for a later send window. It did not show a live send.

### GrokBot Virtual Office: Build a Custom Agent Dashboard
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-virtual-office.html (updated 2026-11-11)
A virtual office is a visual dashboard that shows every bot you run, what each one is doing and which tasks wait for your approval. I built mine in GrokBot by asking my chief of staff bot to create a Page. It shows active, finished and waiting tasks, an event log and a review handoff control for the selected bot, not a native one-click authorization mechanism. You build it the same way: describe the dashboard in plain language, then fix it one request at a time.

### GrokBot vs Dots: Onboarding, Job Drafts and Permissions
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/grokbot-vs-dots.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Both support delegated cloud work, but do not assume the same computer or permission model. In the current GrokBot environment, agents share a persistent Linux box with separate desktops. Dots documentation describes a separate cloud computer for the dot. Dots is accessed through ChatGPT, with availability dependent on the documented plan, region and rollout conditions. GrokBot is xAI's bot app on desktop and iOS, where you can run many bots side by side. In my one head-to-head test, building a job application agent, GrokBot set up a working pipeline in minutes, while my dot took around 45 minutes and could not find contact emails. Try both on your own task before you decide.

### Herdr Desktop Guide: Setup, Workspaces and Limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/herdr-desktop-app.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Install the current official Herdr desktop app, open one repository as a space, and run agents in separate tabs. Closing the window is not the same as stopping herdr-core. The memory figure I saw in my video is one reading on my machine, not a benchmark.

### Herdr Terminal Guide: Workspaces and Coding-Agent Sessions
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/herdr-guide.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Herdr is a free, open source terminal workspace for coding agents. It does not replace Claude Code or Codex. It runs them in panes and tabs, groups them by project, keeps them running in a background server when you close the window, and marks each pane as working, blocked or idle. Install it with curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh, then run herdr in your project folder.

### Self-Host n8n on Hostinger: KVM and First Import

### How to install OpenClaw: local, VPS or hosted, safely
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/install-openclaw.html (updated 2026-11-07)
Run OpenClaw on a VPS, a spare machine or a hosted service rather than your main computer. It can read files and run commands with your account’s permissions. Install it with the official installer: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash on macOS, Linux or WSL2, or iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex in Windows PowerShell. The installer sets up Node.js if needed and starts onboarding. Keep the gateway on localhost, and run openclaw security audit before you connect any accounts.

### Kilo Code tutorial: install, free models and first task
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/kilo-code-tutorial.html (updated 2026-11-08)
Kilo Code is an open-source AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal. Install the VS Code extension (choose Install Pre-Release Version) or run npm install -g @kilocode/cli, sign in with a free Kilo account, and pick a model. You can use free models through Auto Free, your own API keys, local models, or paid credits. The software is free for individuals; model usage is billed separately. Before your first task, check which actions it may run without asking.

### Kimi K2.7 Code in OpenCode: A Site Audit and Its Cost
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/kimi-k2-7-code-opencode-test.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In OpenCode, run /models and pick Kimi K2.7 Code, then give it a codebase-only site audit and ask it to apply the fixes. In my first-day test it audited technical SEO, on-page SEO, content, authority and links, then began fixes such as the www canonical, robots.txt and a bulk script that made about 1,700 URL replacements in blog JSON files. The audit alone cost close to half of what DeepSeek V4 Pro used the whole day before, and I spent about 3 USD and hit my OpenCode Go monthly limit before the fixes were done.

### Lovable Landing Page: Cal.com, Stripe, Domain
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/lovable-landing-page-calcom-stripe-domain.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Write one prompt for your landing page in ChatGPT and paste it into Replit, Lovable and Orchids. I preferred Lovable’s result. Then ask Lovable to connect the booking button to a Cal.com link, add a floating calendar popup, connect Supabase and Stripe, and buy a domain and email address through it. The site went live in under an hour. Stripe was only partly working: the page prices did not match the Stripe products and the buttons still sent visitors to account creation. Replit and Lovable both needed about $25 a month to deploy or use a custom domain.

### Lovable vs Base44 vs Replit: pricing and which to pick
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/lovable-vs-base44-vs-replit.html (updated 2026-11-08)
Pick Lovable for a polished website or front end you want live quickly; Pro starts at $25 a month for 100 credits. Pick Base44 for a simple internal app with sign-in and a database built in; paid plans start at $16 a month billed yearly. Pick Replit if you want a full coding workspace and expect to edit the code yourself; Core is $20 a month with $20 of usage included. All three have a free plan that is enough to build a first version, not to run it for real users.

### Make.com AI Agent: Tally Form Replies and Where It Stalled
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-ai-agent-tally-email.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Make.com open AI Agents (in beta in July 2025), create an agent, connect a model with your API key, write a system prompt and give it a tool for sending email. Trigger it from a Tally form so each submission runs the agent. My agent correctly spotted who wanted a call and drafted a good reply, but it could not send it because scenario inputs were not available on my plan, so the draft was all I got.

### Make.com Lead Scraper: Apify Apollo Actor to Google Sheets
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-apify-apollo-leads-sheet.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Copy the URL of an Apollo people search, then in Make.com create a Google Sheet, run the Apify Apollo actor with a JSON input holding that URL and a limit of 100 leads, get the dataset items, map first name, last name, email, phone, industry, country and city into an array and iterate it into sheet rows. It ran in about 30 seconds. A sheet-name clash had to be fixed first, and the phone column came back wrong, which mattered little because I wanted the emails.

I walks through about ten of the speaker’s own Make.com scenarios: an email auto-responder, Skool members into an email list, a Messenger bot, an Instagram comment reply, a Google Sheets cold-email sender, an Apollo lead scraper, YouTube description and topic generators, and Make’s template library. Most are two to four modules. Treat the auto-reply and cold-email ones carefully, since consent and quality are not covered.

### Make.com Content Builds: Facebook Posts, Ebook and Forms

The Facebook scenario has ChatGPT write a visual post under 150 words, DALL-E 3 make an image from it, an HTTP step fetch the file and the Facebook module publish a photo post, scheduled daily at 10 am. The ebook scenario keeps the title, outline and status in Airtable, creates a Google Doc and loops over chapters with Claude; it needed a new API key after repeated credit errors and ended mid-run with repeated chapter headings. The Fillout scenario watches new form responses and creates Airtable records, or you can use Fillout’s built-in Airtable integration with no Make.com at all.

### Make.com Faceless Videos: JSON2Video and Auto-Posting

My test videos rendered in about 60 to 70 seconds.

### Make.com Gmail Auto-Reply: Watch, Write and Send With AI
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-gmail-ai-auto-reply.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Make.com add a Gmail watch-emails module for unread inbox messages, then an OpenAI create-a-completion module with four messages: a system role, a task description, a reply format and the email text. Add a sleep step so replies are not instant and a send-email module that replies to the sender and saves a copy in Sent. Run it unlinked from the send step first, read the draft, then connect it.

### Make.com Lead Generation: Pitches, Apollo and Google Maps
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-lead-generation-pitches-apollo-maps.html (updated 2026-11-15)
The simplest build runs a Google Maps text search in Make.com (for example marketing agencies in Bangkok, limited to 50), fetches each place’s website and extracts emails from the HTML with a regular expression ChatGPT wrote, adding rows to a Google Sheet. A second build scrapes an Apollo search of about 1,200 owners and founders with an Apify actor, and a third reads contacts from a sheet, researches each organization with Perplexity and drafts a PR pitch that goes to Airtable for review. ### Facebook Messenger Auto-Replies With Make.com and ChatGPT

In Make.com create a scenario with the Facebook Messenger Watch messages trigger and a webhook with a verify token you choose, add an OpenAI create-a-completion module that writes a reply to the incoming text, and a Messenger send-a-message module that returns it. ### How to make money with AI fast: the honest path
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-ai-fast.html (updated 2026-11-14)
there is no dependable fast way to make money with AI. AI makes drafts quick, but income comes from finding a person who wants the result, trusts you to check it and agrees to pay, and that part does not speed up because the tool did. The fastest honest route: pick a task you can check yourself, ask one person who has that task, and deliver one small result.

### Make money with AI with no experience
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-ai-no-experience.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Start with a task you already understand, such as organizing requests or cleaning a spreadsheet. Build the smallest version on free tiers, without AI first, use it on your own work, then offer the narrow version to one person you know. AI helps with parts of the job; customers still pay for your judgment and reliability, and income is not guaranteed.

### Make money with ChatGPT: 4 client services
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-money-with-chatgpt.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Use ChatGPT inside client work you can check yourself: editing documents, research summaries with sources, customer FAQ drafts from approved information, or bounded custom GPT projects. Define the finished deliverable first, review every output before handing it over, and agree on AI use and disclosure with the client. More output is not more value.

### Make.com News-to-Video Autoposter: RSS to Social Posts
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-news-to-video-autoposter.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Add an RSS reader module with a news feed URL and return one item, send it to Perplexity’s Sonar model with a prompt to summarize the article for social posts, and have ChatGPT write a scene-based video script of 30 to 60 seconds with overlay text, voice-over and an English image prompt per scene. Parse the JSON, render it in JSON2Video at 720p with a free Azure voice, fetch the file, have ChatGPT write the post text and use a router to upload to Facebook, Instagram and YouTube. In my test the article was summarized but video creation stopped because my JSON2Video quota was used up.

### Make.com YouTube Description Updater
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-youtube-description-updater.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Make an Airtable table of video titles, URLs, video IDs, a description template, a description field and a status. A Make.com scenario takes one to-do row, fetches the transcript with Dumpling AI, asks an OpenAI assistant to write a description from the transcript and your template, updates the video through the YouTube module and marks the row done. Schedule it every five minutes. Titles stay unchanged, and an OpenAI credit error needed a $6 top-up to fix.

### Make.com YouTube Idea-to-Video Pipeline: Apify to Upload
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/make-youtube-ideas-to-video-pipeline.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Scrape the latest videos from a few creators in your niche with an Apify YouTube channel scraper, save titles, links, durations and views to Airtable sorted by views, and send the top titles to an OpenAI assistant that returns ten ideas in JSON. GPT-4.1 then writes a scene-by-scene script with voice-over and an image prompt per scene, JSON2Video renders a vertical video, and the file uploads to YouTube with the AI-generated label switched on. In my 30-minute build the final run failed because my free JSON2Video quota was used up, so I hardcoded an older render to show the download.

### Wrap Odysseus in an Electron Desktop App With an AI Agent

### OpenCode Go: pricing, models, limits and setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-go.html (updated 2026-11-14)
OpenCode Go is a monthly subscription to a curated set of open and low-cost coding models, run by the team behind OpenCode. Go costs $10 a month, Go Plus $40 a month, and Go Teams $20 per member per month. Each model has its own monthly allowance in dollars, with 20% usable per 5 hours and 50% per week. You connect it in OpenCode with /connect, then pick a model with /models. It is optional: OpenCode itself is free and works with other providers.

### OpenCode Skill That Trims Long Videos Into Shorts
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-video-trim-skill.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Prompt OpenCode to create a skill that turns a long video into a 1.5 to 2.5 minute 16x9 cut that starts on a hook and removes filler words. On a 10-minute tutorial it took about five minutes of CPU to produce a cut of about a minute and a half, and an existing Shorts skill made the 9x16 version in under 30 seconds. ### OpenCode vs Claude Code: pricing, setup and limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/opencode-vs-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-11)
pick Claude Code if you already pay for a Claude plan and want Anthropic’s own coding agent. Pick OpenCode if you want an MIT-licensed, open source agent that can use models from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or local options such as Ollama. Neither is ranked faster here: run the same small task in both and compare setup time, failed requests and the final diff.

### OpenDesign (Open Design) on Linux: Source Setup and Slides

### OpenRouter setup: API key and free models
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/openrouter-setup.html (updated 2026-11-14)
OpenRouter is one API in front of hundreds of models from many providers. Create an account, add credits if you need paid models, and create an API key at openrouter.ai/settings/keys. Then point any OpenAI-compatible tool at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with that key. Free models end in :free and are capped at 50 requests a day, or 1,000 a day once you have bought at least 10 credits. Paid models cost the provider’s listed price; OpenRouter charges a 5.5% fee when you buy credits.

### OpenSEO review: setup, data costs and practical limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/openseo-review.html (updated 2026-11-19)
OpenSEO is worth evaluating for focused SEO research, but its free self-hosted app still needs paid data, and my demo doesn't show it replacing every paid suite.

### Otterly AI Walkthrough: Brand Mentions, Citations, Pricing
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/otterly-ai-visibility-tracking.html (updated 2026-11-19)
On 17 April 2026 I walked an Otterly AI dashboard that tracks a brand in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot. I said it had a 2-week free trial, then about $29 a month. For TubeAnalytics I read about 43 percent brand coverage versus VidIQ around 68 percent, about 20 brand mentions, position four, a visibility index that called us a leader in brand coverage, and about 78 percent likelihood to buy. Crawlability showed crawlers allowed. One prompt maxed at 100. Another scored 67 out of 100 at the top. Those figures are that day's dashboard, not a live rank. TubeAnalytics is my own product. I said the description signup link is a referral, so I earn a commission if you use it.

### Pi.dev Terminal Coding Agent: Install, OpenRouter and Costs
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/pi-dev-terminal-coding-agent.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Install Pi with the one-line npm command from pi.dev, run pi, type login, choose API key and paste an OpenRouter key. It picked Kimi 2.6 by default, and the model list offered about 252 models. I ran a full site audit on my project, used the session command to see messages, tokens and total cost, and also connected Google Cloud Code Assist. Runs were slow, my OpenRouter balance went negative and Gemma 4 free hit a rate limit, so I topped up $5 and turned on auto top-up. I preferred OpenCode.

In Rank Prompt, enter a site, run a visibility scan, pick categories so the product can generate prompts, then read where those prompts show up across the models you selected. The 12 November 2026 walkthrough then installed the Rank Prompt MCP in Claude Code, authenticated with an API key, and used that data to edit pages and draft outreach. Rank Prompt sponsored this video. The on-site edits were not treated as an instant rank change.

I connected REA to my coding agents with its one-line npx setup command, then asked Claude Code to rebuild Kdenlive, my usual video editor. After hours of work it produced a prototype called Cutline. ### Build Viral Post Genie in Replit: Errors, Limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/replit-viral-post-genie-build.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Replit choose Web app, paste a detailed prompt written in ChatGPT and let the agent build it. Mine was Viral Post Genie, a Facebook post generator with a topic, style and call-to-action form. Add an OpenAI key when asked, then fix the errors that follow: max tokens, an unsupported JSON object format and a 500 error, which I cleared by switching to GPT-4. I then added a numbered thread format, a demo popup, AI images, a history and Google sign-in on a temporary Postgres database before hitting the starter plan limit. Deploying needs a paid plan.

### RTK Token Savings: Install, Hooks and Checks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/rtk-token-savings-claude-code.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Install RTK from GitHub with the curl line on that page or with brew install rtk, add it to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, run rtk init so the hook is present, then run rtk gain to read savings. On 21 July 2026, GLM 5.2 showed 169,000 tokens saved.

### GrokBot WordPress Workflow: Long-Form Videos to Drafts
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/run-a-blog-with-grokbot.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Locate the WordPress connector through the app’s supported connection flow. In my video the panel is called Plugins. Connect only the permissions needed for your approved task. Create a blog writer bot and give it a source, such as your YouTube videos. In my video, the bot retrieves transcripts and prepares posts, excerpts, categories and tags, with some items scheduled. For a new setup, request reviewable drafts rather than assuming publication is authorized. Keep the initial workflow draft-only. Scheduling and any subscriber email are separate approvals, not a default result of asking for an article.

### Self-host n8n on Ubuntu: Docker and Node.js setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/self-host-n8n.html (updated 2026-11-14)
For a machine that stays on, use Docker or Docker Compose, which n8n’s docs recommend. npm installs are deprecated from n8n 3.0. The recorded Ubuntu video uses Node.js 24 and npm install n8n -g, which still works for learning on a laptop. Either way, open localhost:5678, create the owner account, and run a three-node test workflow before adding credentials. Self-hosting is free, and this setup is reachable only from your own computer.

Review that plan before you ship anything. This page follows the 6 August 2026 walkthrough. It is not a current Semrush price list.

### SendPulse Facebook Chatbot: Comment Replies and DMs
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/sendpulse-facebook-comment-chatbot.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Connect your Facebook page to SendPulse, create a trigger for comments on any post, add several randomized public replies so you do not look repetitive and send each commenter one direct message. Make the message a yes or no question or a set of link buttons, ignore repeated triggers for 12 hours, tag and log interested people and close the chat. An AI agent step can take over later replies but needed a paid plan. I have used it for about two years on a page of roughly 175,000 to 180,000 followers.

https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/six-agent-builds-claude-code-dashboards-outreach.html (updated 2026-11-15)
These are six prompt-driven builds, mostly first drafts. I set up Claude Code on Debian and in VS Code, built a competitor dashboard with Apify skills in Claude Code (Apify sponsored that one), an Alpaca paper-trading dashboard with free OpenCode models whose chart never rendered, a mock-data AI operating system dashboard, a sponsorship outreach agent in Odysseus and a local lead and website-audit tool called LeadScope. ### Skool Classroom Tour: Free Lessons and Paid Upsells
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-classroom-upsell-tour.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Keep the community free to join, welcome every introduction quickly and put free material in the classroom: a start-here module with guidelines, step-by-step tutorials and short how-to guides. Sell the paid items beside them. Two weeks in, with almost 200 members, mine listed a $39 beginner course, a $97 template pack and a $197 n8n agent pack, plus a book, mentoring calls and a consultation. I said upsells had earned about $500 against Skool’s $99 monthly fee. Those are my own figures.

### Skool Community Setup: Pricing, About Page and Classroom
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-community-setup-guide.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Create the community and choose the $9 Hobby plan (10% fee) or $99 Pro plan (2.9%), both with a 14-day trial. Then set a monthly price or keep it free, add membership questions and categories, write an About page with video and a testimonial, post introductions and polls, and build a classroom with free tutorials plus a paid course. In my September 2025 tour I reported about $700 in one-time sales over three months. The income examples at the start of the video are quoted from Skool pages and not verified.

### A Free Skool Community: What I Did in the First Two Weeks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-free-community-first-weeks.html (updated 2026-11-15)
I launched a free Skool community around Make.com automations and promoted it on Facebook, YouTube and my email list. After about two weeks it had 160 members and ranked on page six of the tech category. Free joining let me collect every new member’s email and send an automatic welcome message. I sell templates, a Make.com course and $150-an-hour consultations inside it, and said I had made about $300 against the $99 monthly fee. Those are my own early figures.

### Skool $9 Hobby Plan vs Pro: Fees, Admins and Limits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-hobby-plan-review.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In July 2025 Skool's Hobby plan was $9 a month with one admin and a 10% transaction fee, and no custom URL, plugins such as Zapier, sidebar links, Facebook pixel or hiding suggested communities. Pro was $99 a month with unlimited admins, a 2.9% fee and those extras. I downgraded two communities to Hobby, paying $18 a month for a free and a paid community, and kept my existing URLs.

### Skool Membership Tiers: Free, Premium and VIP Setup
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-membership-tiers.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In your Skool community open Settings, then Pricing, and switch on membership tiers: a free level plus one or two paid upgrades. In October 2025 I set mine to free, premium at $29 a month ($280 a year) and VIP at $89 a month ($850 a year), then locked classroom modules and live calls to each tier. Skool's Hobby plan was $9 a month with a 10% fee and Pro was $99 with 2.9%, as I noted then.

### Skool Welcome Emails With Zapier, Make.com and EmailOctopus
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/skool-welcome-email-automation.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Skool had no public API in July 2025, so use its Zapier integration to append each new member, with their answers and email, to a Google Sheet. In Make.com watch that sheet for new rows and add each person to EmailOctopus with first name and email, which starts a welcome sequence: an intro email, a 12-hour wait, a second email, a two-day wait and a last email. The catch: once my community became paid, I could no longer ask membership questions, so I could not collect emails from new members that way.

### n8n Music Video Workflow: Suno, Nano Banana Pro, Creatomate
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/suno-n8n-music-video-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Add an n8n form trigger that collects a music genre, have an OpenAI node write a Suno prompt under 500 characters, call the KIE Suno endpoint for instrumental tracks and poll every 10 seconds until the task succeeds. Generate a 16:9, 2K background image with Nano Banana Pro the same way, then render a Creatomate template with the two audio URLs and the image and upload the video to Google Drive. Everything worked up to the Creatomate step, which errored in my demo and still needed debugging. For a one-off channel, making the videos by hand may be easier.

### Syllaby Bulk Scheduler: A Week of Faceless Videos at Once
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/syllaby-bulk-scheduler-faceless-videos.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Syllaby create a faceless video, choose a style, subtitles and voice, then use the bulk option: it generates scripts for 7 to 30 days from a few prompts, renders each video in about 5 to 10 minutes and places them in the content calendar with posts scheduled to YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and other accounts, up to five a day. I quoted 13 credits per minute of video and 500 credits a month on the paid plan, which starts at $25 a month. The script assistant failed with not-found errors several times before it worked.

### Syllaby First Test: A Faceless Video From Idea to YouTube
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/syllaby-faceless-video-first-test.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Syllaby choose Create video, then Faceless video, pick a visual style, subtitles and voice, set portrait and a length under a minute, and write a custom topic for the AI script assistant. I added ambient music and sound effects, rendered the video in about three minutes despite an on-screen application error, then connected YouTube and published straight from Syllaby. The free trial had about 50 credits, roughly three minutes of video. I did not check the AI script’s cost-of-living claims or see how the video performed.

### Trakkr and Codex: AI Visibility, Crawlers and Visits
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/trakkr-codex-visibility-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Connect Trakkr's hosted MCP server to Codex, pull the action list into a report, and read it before you let Codex edit anything. Keep AI visibility, crawler visits, citations and real visitors as separate numbers. An assistant naming your brand is not a click, and a fix list is not a result.

### Treg in GrokBot: Connect Data Tools and Control Costs
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/treg-inside-grokbot.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Treg is a catalog of external APIs that an agent reaches through one connection and one token. To use it in GrokBot, open Plugins in the left sidebar, search for "treg," add it, and sign in. Your bots can then search the catalog by task, see the price of each endpoint, and make the call. You pay per call from a prepaid balance, or connect your own API keys for providers you already pay for.

### Vapi Outbound AI Caller: Twilio, Make.com and Google Sheets
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/vapi-outbound-ai-caller-make-twilio.html (updated 2026-11-15)
Create a Vapi assistant from the appointment scheduler template with OpenAI as the model, pick an ElevenLabs professional clone for the voice and add the book-appointment and check-availability tools. Buy a Twilio number and import it into Vapi with the account SID and auth token. Then build a Make.com scenario that finds unsent rows in Google Sheets, loops over them, creates a Vapi outbound call, marks the row called and waits between calls. My live test call to my own phone booked a calendar slot. Vapi’s outbound campaign feature did not work for me, so Make.com did the dialing.

### Vapi AI tutorial: build a voice agent, test calls, webhooks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/vapi-voice-agent-tutorial.html (updated 2026-11-11)
Vapi is a platform for building voice AI agents: a transcriber turns the caller’s speech into text, a model writes the reply and a voice speaks it. To build one, create an assistant with a first message and system prompt, test it in the dashboard, connect a phone number, then confirm webhook events arrive before adding business actions.

### vidIQ MCP in Claude: Channel Audit and Idea Checks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/vidiq-mcp-claude-channel-audit.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Claude Desktop click the plus icon, choose Add a connector and enter the vidIQ MCP server URL from vidIQ’s MCP page. Then ask for a video idea validation, a full channel audit or a competitor breakdown. Claude calls vidIQ tools for keyword research, outliers and trending videos and answers from real channel data. In my May 2026 test the channel health check first returned the wrong channel, and pasting the channel ID fixed it.

### VisiScan AI Visibility: Free Scan and Report
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/visiscan-ai-visibility-audit.html (updated 2026-11-19)
Enter a domain in VisiScan, run the free scan, and read the readiness and visibility scores. The 22 July 2026 walkthrough also opened sitemap, robots.txt and machine-readable file checks, then showed a paid full report generated in Codex. VisiScan is Mike Holp's own product.

### What is an AI agent? Definition, examples and first build
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent.html (updated 2026-11-11)
An AI agent is software that uses a language model and a set of tools to work toward a goal, choosing its own next step after each result. A workflow follows steps you wrote in advance. Use an agent when the steps cannot be planned ahead, and add checks before it acts.

### What is MCP? The Model Context Protocol explained
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-mcp.html (updated 2026-11-11)
MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard for connecting AI apps to outside tools and data. An app such as Claude Code or Codex connects to MCP servers, and each server offers tools the model can call. Anthropic open-sourced it in November 2024, and ChatGPT, VS Code and Cursor support it too.

### What is n8n used for? Real uses and a first workflow
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/what-is-n8n-used-for.html (updated 2026-11-08)
n8n is a workflow automation tool. You connect apps, APIs and AI models on a visual canvas, and n8n runs the steps when something happens. This guide lists jobs people hand to it and a first workflow you can check.

### WhatsApp AI Voice Clone in Make.com: Texts and Voice Memos
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/whatsapp-ai-voice-clone-make.html (updated 2026-11-15)
In Make.com add a WhatsApp Business Cloud watch-events trigger and a router with filters for text and audio messages. Create an OpenAI assistant with a short role prompt and a vector store of your YouTube transcripts, built by a second scenario that reads links from Google Sheets, fetches transcripts with Dumpling AI, saves them to Google Drive and uploads them. Make an instant ElevenLabs clone, generate speech with the multilingual model and send it as a WhatsApp audio message. In my test the router filters went missing and had to be re-added, and the number was hardcoded.

### YouTube channel growth workflow: research, publish, learn
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-channel-growth-workflow.html (updated 2026-11-14)
choose an idea for a specific viewer, make the title and thumbnail promise clear, publish a video that keeps that promise, then use several analytics signals to decide what to improve. A single view count or competitor estimate cannot tell you why a video performed as it did.

### React YouTube feed tutorial: API, caching and fallbacks
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-feed.html (updated 2026-11-14)
Fetch your uploads on the server, keep a saved list as a fallback, and render that list into the HTML so the page still shows watch links and thumbnails when the YouTube request fails, then refresh it in the browser. Check the result by making the live fetch fail on purpose and confirming the videos still appear.

### YouTube to LinkedIn Automations in n8n and OpenCode
https://www.ai-automation-station.com/guides/youtube-to-linkedin-automations-n8n-opencode.html (updated 2026-11-15)
All four builds start from a video transcript and end with copy you review and post yourself. The simplest n8n version watches your channel’s RSS feed, pulls the transcript with an Apify actor, joins the pieces and asks Claude for a 400-word newsletter saved to Google Docs. The fuller versions add a Gemini summary and a 4K or 2K infographic from Nano Banana Pro through KIE, with a polling loop. A fourth build uses OpenCode and DeepSeek V4 Flash to write a script that makes five LinkedIn post variants from a video. I do not automate the posting step.
